utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: This Status Conference is called to order. Good afternoon to everybody. Madam Registrar, would you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon. This is case number IT-95-14-A, Prosecutor versus Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. May I call for the appearances. For the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Appearing for the Prosecution today is myself, Norman Farrell. With me is Ms. Kelly Howick, and our case manager, Wolfgang Sakulin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. For Mr. Blaskic? I understand there is a phone link with counsel for Mr. Blaskic. Is that correct? I don't hear anything at the moment. May I ask for appearance of counsel for Mr. Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon. Appearing for General Blaskic, by telephone from Los Angeles, are Russel Hayman and Andrew Paley.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, Mr. Blaskic, I'm sorry, I didn't ask you before. Did you hear? Do you have any problems with hearing what's going on and with the translation? THE APPELLANT: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I can hear you very well and I can understand everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Now, let us come to the subject of this Status Conference. First, as usual, the Status Conference has the purpose of allowing the appellant to raise any issues in relation to his detention. May I ask if there is any problem of this kind?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is Mr. Hayman. We are not aware of any problems with General Blaskic's issue of detention, but we invite you to address him directly regarding that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hayman. Mr. Blaskic, do you have any complaint to make or any comment to make about your detention? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no complaint about the conditions of detention, and as for comments, all I can say is that the staff is treating everyone professionally and in an equal manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaskic. You know that if you had any problem, you can always follow the procedure under the rules to raise it appropriately. If there is no problem of this kind concerning the detention of Mr. Blaskic, I would like to come to the status of this appeal. Now, I understand that the -- all the briefs, the appeal briefs, are now in. The appellant briefs had been filed in January, and the public redacted version has been filed on the 7th of March. The Prosecution respondent brief was filed on the 1st of May, and the reply of the appellant has been filed today, as it was scheduled. Now, here I see one point I would raise immediately, and that's Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the confidentiality of all these documents. As I told before, the appellant's brief has been filed in a public redacted version on the 7th of March, but we still do not have a public redacted version of the Prosecution's response brief, and of course of the today's reply. I would like to have both these documents in a public redacted version since it is normal that submissions be filed confidentially, only as far as there is a real security concern. Would that be suitable for the parties to have ten days to submit a public redacted version, Mr. Farrell?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: On behalf of the Prosecution, that should be no problem at all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hayman, do you have any problem in filing a public redacted version of the reply, of your reply that was filed today in ten days as of now?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: In ten working days, Your Honour, I am confident we could accomplish that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Ten working days. Okay. Okay, that's fine. So public redacted versions of the Prosecution's respondent brief and of the reply will be filed within ten working days. Coming to the pending motions in this appeal, we have still two pending motions concerning additional evidence. The -- there is a first motion to admit additional evidence submitted by the appellant, to which response and reply have been filed. I note that public redacted version of these briefs have been filed also. A second motion to admit additional evidence has been filed by the appellant. Response and reply have been filed. And public redacted version have been filed of these two documents. So this is fine. I note that the appellant has expressed the intention of filing a third motion for additional evidence. May I, perhaps, ask Mr. Hayman if he can say when such a motion will be filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. Now that we have filed the reply brief today, I expect we can file our third Rule 115 motion no later than Friday, June 7th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. So I understand that motion will be filed at the end of this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: When we will receive that motion, the appeal Chamber has the intention of dealing with these three motions together and issue one decision concerning additional evidence. I cannot say exactly when that decision will be issued, but as soon as possible. Is there any comment in this connection from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: No, none whatsoever, just note that once we receive it, we'll try and comply within the ten days, but we may, depending on the motion itself, seek an extension. But that will be decided at the time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farrell. Mr. Hayman, do you have any comment on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we certainly support that schedule. I do note that we have received some new translated material and other new material within the past few days and weeks from the Prosecution's office pursuant to Rule 68, and now that we again have filed and completed our reply brief today, we will set ourselves immediately to reviewing those materials. Without knowing what is in those materials, I do not know if there is any other material that we need to bring to the attention of the Court under Rule 115. We will not wait, however, to review those further materials to file the Rule 115 motion that we have briefly discussed and raised with the Court with respect to the need for protective measures. So we will get that motion filed this week and proceed from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hayman. I take note of that. And as I said before, the intention of the Chamber is to consider the three motions together. Of course, if you will file additional materials, we will take that into account maybe later, at a later stage possibly, depending on when the material is submitted, of course. Well, this was what I wanted to deal with, with the pending motions. Is there any other issue that the parties would like to raise at this point? Mr. Farrell?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: None on behalf of the Prosecution. No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: None, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I think we can adjourn this Status Conference. The Status Conference stands adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
